title: Compatibility Chaos Lab: flag-matrix fuzzing & golden-prompt regression scanner
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Build an automated compatibility chaos lab that systematically fuzzes combinations of behavior flags, API version gates, and model variants against a curated golden-prompt suite (including streaming/toolcall/structured-output scenarios). The lab will detect regressions, produce actionable diffs (tokens, timing, structured schema mismatches), and auto-open mitigation tickets with repro artifacts. This addresses flaky regressions that slip through unit/integration tests when we change runtime kernels, behavior flags, or client-side expectations.
acceptance_criteria: A nightly job executes a configurable flag-matrix (min 50 permutations) across the golden-prompt suite and records structured outputs and latency distributions for each run
The system computes a regression score per permutation comparing to a baseline and flags any permutation with a score >= threshold

For flagged regressions, the lab attaches: reproduction prompt, raw token stream, structured parse failure trace, runtime config (flag values, model variant, kernel hints), and a permalink to the run in the dashboard
Auto-created Linear issues for confirmed regressions include labels, suggested rollback candidates, and the minimal reproducer permutation
Results are retained for 90 days behind the console dashboard and integrated into PR gating for changes touching behavior flags or runtime selection codepath
next_steps: Finalize golden-prompt suite (selection matrix across streaming, tool-calls, function-return schemas, and edge-length contexts)
Define regression scoring algorithm (token-diff weighting, structured-parse penalties, latency SLO breaches)
Prototype runner that can spawn sandboxes with specific flag sets and model variants (use dedicated infra pool)
Integrate run summaries with Console dashboard and add a minimal webhook to auto-open Linear tickets
